content.text: Hyakunin Isshu (ç™¾äººä¸€é¦– - 'One Hundred People, One Poem Each') is a traditional Japanese card game based on a classical anthology of waka poems. It is played as a competitive game called 'Karuta'. Players must match a poem being read aloud with the correct 'grabbing' card spread out on the floor. It is a game of extreme speed, memory, and auditory processing.
The anthology was compiled by Fujiwara no Teika in the 13th century. The game form, 'Kyogu Karuta', developed during the Edo period.
100 poetry cards. In a match, only 50 are used (25 for each player).
Uta-garuta deck (200 cards: 100 Yomifuda reading cards, 100 Torifuda grabbing cards), playing mat or flat surface, reader (yomite) to read the poems.

Shuffle the 100 Torifuda (grabbing cards). Each player places 25 cards in their territory (face-up). The remaining 50 Torifuda are not used in that round. The Yomifuda (reading deck) is kept separate for the reader.

items.text: Kyōgi Karuta (Competitive): Official competitive rules: 50 Torifuda in play (25 per player), reader reads from full Yomifuda set, strict otetsuki penalty, national rules (e.g. All Japan Karuta Association).
Casual Uta-garuta: Recreational play: may use fewer cards, relaxed reading speed, or team play with multiple players.
Genpei War (Team): Team variant: two teams face each other; reader reads; first correct touch from either team wins the card for that team.
